## Course Description

This course is an introductory course to structural equation modeling (SEM). Throughout the course, we will build on regression fundamentals to build models that capture more complicated relationships than standard regression and which can be applied to a wider variety of use cases beyond basic predictive modeling. 

The core focus will be on path analysis, confirmatory factor analysis, and full latent variable path analysis. As we approach each model, we will discuss how to specify, identify, fit, and report on the models we build. 

The focus of this course will be hands-on and lab oriented. 

## Learning Objectives

By the end of this course, students will:

- Understand the kinds of research questions that can and cannot be answered by SEM models. 
- Build path analysis, confirmatory factor analysis and latent variable path analysis models with academic rigor
- Apply foundational knowledge of SEM to their own research projects

## Required Materials

- No textbooks are required. Readings are linked in the course schedule.
- Laptop with internet connection



## Course Policies

### Attendance

This class is discussion and lab focused. In-person attendance & active participation are expected. In-class work, labs, quizzes, etc may be assigned in class and cannot be made up if the student is not present. 

Class materials (slide decks and other materials) will be provided by the instructor and made available through the EDEP 625 website. Preparatory materisl will be linked. 

Assignments are expected to be handed in on time except. You are welcome to work with other students on homework, although you are expected to submit your own work with explanations in your own words.

## Assignments

Preparatory materials: These are readings or videos that introduce the topics we'll cover in class and should be done prior to class. 

In-class assignments: throught the semester, students will complete assignments in class.

Labs: Most weeks part of the class time we will be labs, which are an opportunity for you to apply what we discuss in class and build models.

Data search: You will need one or more large datasets from your field that you can use for mini projects. Details and requirements will be forthcoming. 

Mini projects: Instead of a final paper, students will complete three mini projects on the three key models covered. This will be an extension of in-class labs we do and will rely on questions and data relevant to the student's field. These are not full research papers. Details will be forthcoming. 

Research connections: Students will identify papers in their field that use one of the three key models discussed in the class and will present it to the class. Students will also keep information on classmates' presentations in order to better understand how SEM models are used in a variety of fields and contexts. 

Review: While not formally graded, students are expected to spend a few hours each week reviewing course materials, labs, and otherwise solidifying their understanding of SEM. Students are encouraged to form study groups for this.

## Grading

| Component | Weight |
|---|---|
| In-class work | [10%] |
| Labs | [10%] |
| Data search | [10%] |
| Research connections | [10%] |
| Mini project 1 | [20%] |
| Mini project 2 | [20%] |
| Mini project 3 | [20%] |
